utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll read to you now a part of your testimony of the 27th November. Since the transcript I'm reading is in English, I'll read in English, and the interpreters will interpret it for you. The page in question is 4619, lines 13 to 16 in the transcript: [In English] "And then Ljubisa and sometimes Stevica or Beg, Sabahudin and then Sejdinovic, they changed, and they would come outside with small pieces of paper and they would read out the names of 20 or 30 people and say: You are going to dig trenches in Pisarevici, you are going to Crkvina, you are going to do this or that." Did you say this, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, please tell me: This gentleman, Beg, this Sabahudin Nogic and Sejdinovic, all of them are Muslims, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will read to you another part of your testimony before this Court. It's about the beginning of July, when you, too, were asked to report for work duty. The transcript date 27th of November, page 4625, lines 23 to 25.: [In English] First, the question was: "Did you report somewhere to be given a work assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first a courier named Rasovic [phoen] came to my house, and he brought me a small piece of paper, a summons, telling me to report to the local community the following morning. Some woman had already been going to milk cows since April, so I reported to the local community. When I arrived, I went to see Beg, Beg. That was Kapetanovic. I don't know his first name. And I said: What's all this? And he said: From now on -- and then he whispered: Until better times, you will report every morning at 7.00 or 8.00, depending on when the curfew ends, here in front of the local commune, and you will be given a work assignment."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That man was a Muslim, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P39 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We seem to have a problem in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Line 19, you mean, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The question was: Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness did answer "yes." All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, having heard what I've just read, I asked you: Is that what you said? Did you say that? And your answer was yes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. May I see the document first? I'm really sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do we go back into closed session if they're going to place it on the ELMO? I'm very sorry. Do we go back into closed session if it's going to be placed on the ELMO or private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is exactly why I wanted to see the document, Your Honours, just to make sure that we don't have to go into the closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, we don't have to go into the private session, Your Honour -- closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you want it on the ELMO or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just for the purposes of -- everybody can see, it's just a name which doesn't have anything to do with this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to read what is written in the top left corner, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please take the document closer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clerks of the 1st DB for duties of work brigades, data on the method, conditions, and funds for the payment of salaries according to established coefficients for the months of April, May, June, and July of 1992." If you could please raise it a bit. This list -- you've asked me. I want to explain. If you could now move it to the left, please. So in the signature, it's the president of the executive board who is indicated, Milan Simic, economist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it this Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean if the signature is identical?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have to explain what you are reading.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this was drafted on the orders of the president of the executive board, Milan Simic, and it was signed by him. And now move it to the right, please. The value of the coefficient is missing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, may I lead the witness in this? Because I would not like to intimidate the witness, to cut her short, but I mean, I don't need all the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- all the data which is contained in this document. We are losing time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, wait for questions from counsel on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, madam. I'll try to go through this document at our own pace. Tell me, please: The first column are numbers; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There are nine numbers, referring to nine persons; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This person under number 1, Sejfudin Sejdinovic, you have already said he was a Muslim and he was a clerk in the work brigade, the labour brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a clerk from the month of August onwards, and in the month of July, he went with me to Kornica to establish the prevailing conditions in agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The gentleman under number 2, he was also the same, clerk for work obligations, Dzevad Celic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in the month of September he was a clerk, indeed. I know that from my son, who told me. But from the date when I was taken to Zasavica - and I know this firsthand - he went to dig trenches and do other work, that is, labour, and he was not a clerk in this particular Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, between their jobs, as indicated, and their names, are certain numbers. Can you tell me what they mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the months?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I mean this number here, what does it designate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of working days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This number of working days means the same thing for all the other persons on this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the period indicated in the title for this number of months.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The document so we can see the rest --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Usher, can you move the document just a bit so we can see the rest of the document, the right side of the document? No, the right side. The other. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here in the last column, under the heading "dinars," certain amounts are indicated; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The amount for Mr. Sejfudin Sejdinovic is 18.450; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As you understand this document, that means dinars; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, does this represent remuneration for their work; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me whether it represents it or whether they got it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking whether it represents remuneration.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may represent it, but we can't see from this whether they actually got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These amounts of remuneration vary depending on the number of working days; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I didn't dispute that. What I was trying to dispute --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, please. Tell me about these nine persons. Are they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I don't need this document any more. However, I would like you to present another document to the witness. I am sorry. It's D23/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there a problem with the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document can be also put on the ELMO. It's practically the same people who are on the previous document are on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The usher will just put this on the ELMO, please. Could you please read for me the title of this document, if you can see it well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Payroll of clerks, the typist, couriers delivering summons, and couriers in charge of work organisation in the labour brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, can you tell us whether the same persons are indicated as in the previous document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dzevad Celic ... Yes. The only difference is they were grouped according to their occupation, their trade. It's the same group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: In the line where Sejfudin Sejdinovic is indicated, the column "total days" includes number 123?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm telling you, he wasn't a clerk at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the number is identical to the one in the previous document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the same is true of the gentleman under number 2, who was a clerk, and you claim he was not at that time, the number indicated is the same as in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the bottom of the page. Do you see here in the bottom right-hand corner something is written, and there is a signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Authorised by Sejfudin Sejdinovic." That's the signature. Or "approved by."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejfudin Sejdinovic was -- is the clerk under number 1 in this document; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I don't need this document any more. [Interpretation] Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Zecevic. Sorry. I apologise for mispronouncing your names. I wonder whether I could put a question to yourself. Putting to one side for the moment the issue of the legal status of laws of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in Bosnia and Herzegovina since its declaration of independence in February 1992, putting that to one side, is it your position that such work assignments as given to this witness, previous witnesses, and so on, which appear to a great extent to have been under armed guard, whether it's digging trenches or in the fields or what have you, complied with the laws of the former Yugoslavia concerning work obligation and so on, if people voluntarily showed up at the local commune, as this witness has indicated to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may, very briefly, Your Honours. It is exactly our understanding that this working obligation - and, I mean, this is what we are going to prove in this case - that this working obligation was in completely complying with the laws of the former Yugoslavia and the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time. But we are not talking about that, because I would not like to prejudice something. It is our understanding, on the other hand, that the voluntarism is not an issue, because according to the laws at the time, it was the obligation of each and every citizen of the former Yugoslavia to be included either in the military or working obligation. So if he's not a male within 18 to 60, or for whatever other reason was not included into the military obligation, he was obliged to take part in the working obligation. On the other hand, the third question: The guards, the guard who was accompanying these witnesses, in our understanding, was there to protect them and not to guard them. And there were also -- we heard evidence of I believe previous witness was actually -- has actually confirmed that these guards were not guarding them, but they would bring them to the trenches, and then the military unit which is on the trenches is actually giving them assignment and all that. Thank you. And I believe it's time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall break for our lunch break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, may I raise one brief issue regarding the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's only this: I wonder if my learned friends could give me an indication when they expect to finish, because the witness is currently at the hotel. That's the first matter that I would ask. And secondly, can I foreshadow a possible application for some sort of protective measures in respect of the next witness that I understand have not yet been made. He raised the issue with me last night, briefly. I intend to see him over the break at the hotel and see what he wants to say about the matter and find out from him what the issues are, and I just thought I would foreshadow a possible application so that my learned friends and the Chamber is aware that that may be coming from the Prosecution before he gives his evidence. But if the Defence counsel could let the Chamber know approximately when they expect to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zecevic, how long --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately, I don't have the slightest idea, because I have -- this is, of course, not my witness. I am cross-examining the Prosecutor's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we have seen yesterday the level of control that can be established over this witness. That is one aspect. I assumed that until now I will use only 20 minutes, and I have used over an hour, just because of the way how the witness is answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I cannot really say anything. I believe that I will need another hour, but really, don't take me for my word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It might be even three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: May I just make one point in reminder. I think that if there have been answers favourable to yourselves from a primary witness like the husband, then perhaps cross-examination of this witness in respect of the same material may well be controlled, because the primary witness is the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I'm cross-examining the witness on the basis of the examination-in-chief which was conducted by my learned friend yesterday, and the same documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I'm making a general remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: There's no personal remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I've been following your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, it doesn't look like --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It doesn't look like we'll finish this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- if more counsel have to follow on from Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because there are two -- yes. Mr. Lukic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not be cross-examining this witness. I can say this on behalf of the Defence team of Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So maybe we can ask Mr. Pantelic how long he thinks he will need.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have only slight questions and clarifications with regard to the transcript and to the previous statement during the examination-in-chief, so I will not take more than 20 minutes. And I hope that this charming lady will be very cooperative, so we shall be limited with yes or no answers, and under these conditions, I think 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll have the witness ready here on standby just in case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll resume the proceedings at 1530 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.06 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session, I think. We have had to start late because of administrative and security problems in getting the accused into the courtroom. Yes, Mr. Zecevic, you can continue cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam, once again. Madam, during your testimony, you have said several times that you worked at the self-interest community as a clerk; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in various self-interest groups, and that's where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's globally described and administrative described kind of work what a clerk does?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an administrative kind of work, it also involves some accounting work, and I also worked as a clerk for national defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me paraphrase my question. Since you were a clerk, do you believe that the clerks are those who in a way organise the work within the scope of their job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And they also implement it, don't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about the clerks in these municipal groups that she worked in in the 70s and '80s? Is that -- I don't see the relevance to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the relevance, my dear colleague, is that this lady here was employed as a clerk for five years, so she is very competent to say what is the business of a clerk, in general. And while we are talking about these lists, the previous documents which I showed, there are two clerks, and that was the relevance of this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I've got no objection to going over her background as a clerk, but if he's going to try and say that these clerks that she saw on those lists do the same work, then I've got a problem with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I never posed that question, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to do it preventively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It did appear as though you were trying to say that she did that job and there were those clerks on that list, maybe the details of their work assignments were similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I was just referring to the general sense what the clerk does. I'm not referring to anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I will read you now a segment from the transcript of the 27th of November. It will be in English. This is a transcript page 4628, dated 27th November, lines 14 and 15. When asked by the Prosecutor:

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And these people, these hundred people or so, of what ethnic group did they belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly Muslim, and some were Croats or children of mixed marriages, for instance, Croat/Serbian," [Interpretation] So this question and answer were given in the context of the work obligation. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, and on the following page of the same transcript, page 4630, lines 20 to 25, you said the following: [In English] "There were more cases like that, more occasions like that. Mr. Jasenica Dzemal came to pick women for forced labour. Although I would not like to use that particular term, although it was exactly what it was, because I certainly wouldn't go gathering, harvesting corn or sweeping streets unless I was forced to. He needed slaves, literally slaves, to go and clean his house and his cellar."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But prior to that I said that he was the one who called us slaves. I didn't call myself a slave. Mr. Dzemal Jasenica, known as Andra, called us slaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was exactly what I was going to ask you. So he was the one who called you slaves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: That certainly hurt you. It is a very insulting term, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: This gentleman, Jasenica Dzemal, is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about his ethnic background. He was a Muslim, wasn't he? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he was addressing women who were mostly Muslims and Croats. There were perhaps few Serbs from mixed marriages, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: He addressed both men and women.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: On page 4631 of the transcript of the 27th of November, line --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Line 17, 18, [Interpretation] You said the following when asked by the Prosecutor: [In English] "You referred to being known as Slavs -- slaves, probably. When anyone ever asked for help for their personal home, did they ever use the word slaves? Did they ever ask using the word slaves?" And your answer was: "I never heard anyone saying that except Mr. Dzemal Jasenica, nicknamed Andra." [Interpretation] Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So madam, nobody else called you slaves except this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I didn't say anything contrary to that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that you said anything to the contrary. I simply wanted to point out his ethnic background, because it is very important, in view of the questions put by the Prosecutor. Please tell me: In the transcript of that same day, page 4632, lines 9 to 12, when asked by the Prosecutor -- let me just describe the context. We were talking about the work obligation once again and you were saying how you were forced to clean. When asked by the Prosecutor:

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were members of the Serb nationality ever assigned to cleaning duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know. There was only one little girl from a mixed marriage. [Interpretation] Is that what you stated, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, please tell me whether you know that the work obligation existed in companies and in institutions as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that when we say "institutions", that also pertains to the health centre of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown a document by the Prosecutor. If you remember, there was a document from the health centre in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could the usher please show the witness D22B/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at the document, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: This document pertains to the health centre of Bosanski Samac? Doesn't that say so in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it pertains to the data on methods, conditions, and means for paying out salaries in accordance with the established coefficients for the month of June 1992; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document contains names, description of jobs, coefficient, and also the amount of remuneration in dinars for all of the people listed in this document; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, so sorry. Would the usher be so kind to show the witness the documents D22A/2 ter and D22C/2 ter. Would you be so kind first to give the witness the document with "A." Okay. Thank you. And you can leave the document -- the "B" document on the table. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, please take a look at these two documents. I don't think you've seen them so far. Have you looked at them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that these are almost identical documents but for different months; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: May and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I meant identical to the previous document which was for the month of June. Could you compare them, please. I have in mind for you to compare the document D22B/2 ter with the others.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So we agree that those are basically identical documents but just pertaining to different months, May, June, and July of 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know if this can be called a document. I see in front of myself a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll accept that it be called a list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say anything about these, because I didn't see them during the war, and they don't look to me as lists which I used to deal with, and they don't look like what I'm used to in terms of payroll lists. So unless I really have to, I wouldn't comment on them. And these people are mostly the employees of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I understand that you are not an expert on this, and I don't ask that you confirm authenticity of these documents. All I'm asking is that you read this out, as you did yesterday for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you want me to read them, there's no problem, but I don't see any need for that, because all of you have the same documents in front of you. But if you insist, I will read. Just tell me which document you want me to read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will the usher please put the document D22A/2 ter on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is no microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The document you're asking for is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That's right. Because the previous witness -- I'm sorry. I forgot. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, would you be so kind and look at the document for the month of May, D22A/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the number of the document. Would you like me to read this out?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will ask questions, just in order to speed it up. Could you please read what it says in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Name of the institution, health centre, Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Data on methods, conditions, and means for paying out salaries based on established coefficients for the month of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Under number 1, we have Dr. Mesud Nogic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coordinator, obstetrician and gynaecologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So coordinator, gynaecologist, and obstetrician is his job description, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this, yes. I really don't know what Dr. Mesud Nogic did during the war in this month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, madam: If we continue on that same line, we have a coefficient, 1.45, and an amount in dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this last amount that you just mentioned, do you suppose that this was his remuneration for the month of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you anything about it, whether that was remuneration or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me now: These four names under the names of Mr. Nogic, the physicians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Ruza Hercinovic, Damir, Dr. Jusufovic, Lirija. Yes, there are four names here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, madam, based on your knowledge, do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, madam: Ruza Hercinovic is a Croat, is she?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the other three physicians whose names you read out are Muslim, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, madam: Have you ever heard that Dr. Nogic or any other physician that you just read out had been arrested during 1992 in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, none of them were arrested, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that in your statement you said that on the day when your husband was arrested, on the 11th of August, you went to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to see the doctor listed as number 3 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it Dr. Damir Hercinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Damir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So as far as you know, they were not forced to work at the health centre as detainees, but if I could call them that, they were simply citizens who had their freedom and continued to work at the same kind of job they had prior to April 17th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think the only question he can ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The only question he can ask, at first, to start off, to establish a basis, whether or not she is aware if these people, these doctors, were forced to work, and then he's trying to add certain comments that these people weren't forced to work and trying to make some other comments in addition to that. We don't even know what knowledge, if any, she has with regard to doctors, whether doctors were forced to work at the health centre. I think a foundation should be laid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I posed the question: So far as you know. If this is known by this witness, the witness can say no, I don't know, or something like that. But she answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you're saying she has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I have heard that she says yes, but it's not in the transcript. But I can -- I can pose the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because I was looking for it. They didn't have it. But you heard Mr. Weiner's point. Okay. You did explain what the basis of your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I believe it's quite appropriate to pose the question like that. Because I'm not insinuating anything. I'm just asking whether she knows this. And I'm posing the question in this manner just to save time, because I can pose in three questions the same question. I'm just trying to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's asking a double question: Were they forced to work or were they citizens who had their freedom and continued to work voluntarily. So if she says yes, does that mean yes, they were forced to work, or yes, they were citizens who maintained their freedom and continued to work voluntarily? The question is -- you know, you can ask the question one question at a time, but first there should be a foundation laid: Does she know whether or not these people were forced to work, does she know them and were they forced to work, and then he can ask the second question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Zecevic, separate your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't really -- I just tried to save the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, please, we have to slice this question into three subquestions. If I understood you properly, you know that they were not detained, they were not detainees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I replied by saying yes, I know that they had not been detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were forced to work at the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, in the months of May, June, July, August of 1992, did they work in their jobs which they had prior to 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some of them, and I can tell you about those that I saw: Dr. Ruza Brdar [phoen] was not working as a pediatrician. She went to visit the detainees and she worked at the emergency centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about the first five individuals on the list. They were physicians. Did they work as physicians during those five months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were physicians, but I don't know if they worked in their jobs. As you know, they are pediatricians, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you mean that there are various specialisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I meant, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, their work after 17th of April, 1992, was it performed within the general work obligation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only suppose. I cannot claim with certainty. They probably did have the work obligation that we talked about before, the work obligation within their enterprise. It certainly would be preposterous to expect a physician to work as a cleaner, and I cannot claim anything that I have not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that you've mentioned cleaning, sweeping, would you be so kind to turn to the second page of that document and to read out two names next to last on that list, and their jobs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bozic, Mizda and Petrovic Mara, janitors of the health centre, and indeed they were janitors of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one is that document? Because she is looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is D22A/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because I was referring to the same document that we were talking about, Your Honours. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, please tell me: These two ladies, cleaning ladies or janitors at the health centre, what was their ethnic background, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you say that their names look like Serbian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, either Serbian or Croatian. I'm not obsessed by various nationalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand you entirely. I'm not obsessed either.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we agree on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me this: The name next to last is Mara Petrovic, and wouldn't you say it's a typical Serbian last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let us continue. I heard, you know, the name Mara exists both in Croatian and Serbian communities. So I can tell you with certainty when the name is a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to the first page of that same document, D22A/2 ter. Yesterday, when you talked to the Prosecutor about a document identified with the same number but with the letter "B," you could not explain what the column identified with PL, full stop, RAS full stop, means.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you what it means today either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that this could mean a salary category?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could mean that. It's a bit clearer to me, because there are some numbers here, and yesterday's document did not contain any numbers at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I keep wondering when you are really going into details with these documents which the witness never saw, she didn't work with these documents, and you're trying to suggest to her what these abbreviations might mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, these documents, in my opinion, are very important. First of all, the -- and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the witness appears to be competent to understand these documents, although she never saw them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but when she says that she doesn't know what an abbreviation means, so you can't suggest to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was just asking whether she would agree with me that it might be this abbreviation of this, and she says yes. I'm trying to remind the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope she doesn't get misled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you have my word, she was not misled in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner, do you see a stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is the stamp familiar to you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does it resemble a stamp from the SDK, the government auditing agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you now, but very briefly, please, explain for the Trial Chamber what the SDK is, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the service of payment -- for payment operations which affixes its stamp on payment orders which serves to transfer money from one giro account to another giro account, from one user of funds to another user. The SDK, however, never affixed their stamp to a payroll. They did on payment orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I completely agree with you. Would you tell me, just very briefly, what the SDK was as opposed to the SPP in the former Yugoslavia, the SDK being the government auditing agency and the SPP being the payment transaction service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you want -- if you know what it is, then you can explain it. If I -- if you didn't know, then I would understand why I needed to explain it to you. You know that the service for payment operations is the service through which all payments are carried out. I don't know what other explanation you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question, then. Is it true that in the former Yugoslavia, all payment transactions went through that service and not through banks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even to this day, payment transactions go -- went until recently through these services, the SDK and the SPP, rather than banks, and payments only since recently go through banks. But I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you mean -- when you say "in this state," you mean in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the Republika Srpska as well, but I mean mainly the Republic of Bosnia. I'm sorry I have to waste everybody's time here. Because you know what I mean. Bosnia and the Federation, those are not states. The Republika Srpska and the Federation constitute the state together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right, madam. Just one more question about this. So work organisations or enterprises would deliver their payment orders to the payment transaction service for various payments, including payrolls, and these were approved and implemented, so these payment orders were effected on behalf of enterprises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to explain how it went and then you can clarify it? You make a calculation of all the salaries. You sum up gross salaries and net salaries. Gross salaries include various contributions for health insurance, education, culture, et cetera. You deduct these, and for each of these items you make an order that the gross net -- you make these deductions and then you make an order to transfer these funds to the relevant organisations for education, health, et cetera. And then, as far as net salaries are concerned, they are paid out to workers according to a list. They have to sign against their name. If some workers have their own bank accounts, the money is paid by a payment order to this bank account. It makes absolutely no sense that the SDK should affix a stamp on a list like this. Why, then, is there no such stamp on the other lists we have here? You want me to interpret financial matters here. If you want me to do that, you will have to pay me as an expert. If you ask my personal opinion, what we have here is not a payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, let me say just one thing. I wasn't claiming that this is a payroll. Even the title itself says "data," not payroll?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'll read it once again. Data on the mode, conditions, and funds for the payment of salaries according to established coefficient for the month of May. We cannot see what the mode is, we cannot see what the conditions are for these calculations, we cannot see what kind of funds these are. It may be cash, it may be in the form of goods, so it's a payroll of sorts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness shouldn't be bothered with all this, like I've said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Neither are we. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These are not --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These are not her documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know these are not her documents. I'm just trying to explain to this Honourable Trial Chamber what this document contains, but -- anyhow, I will withdraw that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think you can do that with the authors of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me -- excuse me, Mr. Zecevic. I wonder whether either yourself or the witness could I think assist the Chamber by giving us some indication, if possible, as to who or whom decided which persons should show up to the commune each day and be assigned to go off to fields or clean, what have you, on the one hand; and on the other hand, which people should remain in the institutional businesses or set-ups where they worked on a regular basis. How was this decided?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Shall I ask the witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, you have heard this last question. You have understood it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will you then be so kind as to answer: Who decided things like who was going to do work obligation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And do you happen to know who decided that certain individuals would be working in enterprises or institutions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe you're not satisfied, of course, but would you like me to clarify that or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Not necessarily right now, but I think it's something that at some stage it would be very important for us to be informed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question regarding these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We've lost counsel's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said yesterday that the documents don't look authentic because they were not written in Cyrillic script. But I understand they were typed in a Latinic -- on a Latinic typewriter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was referring to a typed document. I think there was a mixture of both on the document that I was looking at, but I'm a fairly well educated woman. I understand both scripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know. Tell me, madam: While you were working at this self-interest community, Cyrillic typewriters were a rarity, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have one, that's for sure. I don't know whether they were a rarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone own a Cyrillic typewriter at your employer's organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, neither in the self-interest community where I worked before or in my later employer's organisation, we didn't have such a typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will you take now document 22C ter -- /2 ter, the list for July. It is written in Cyrillic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, there is something strange. The column "total" is written in the Latinic script. That's funny.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, against the name of Mesud Nogic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me find it. Here he is, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Against the names of the other doctors, the number of working days is indicated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: July 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under number 5, Dr. Sladjana Mihaljcic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the number, but I can count, yes. I can see her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, madam: If you look at her coefficient and the amount of her remuneration in dinars, did it differ in any way from that of her colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amounts all look the same, apart from Dr. Mesud Nogic. I don't know really. If you ask me --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more thing regarding this work obligation and we'll be finished. When you were testifying yesterday, on the 28th of November, page 11 of the unofficial transcript, lines 2 to 5, in response to a question by the Prosecutor regarding the period after the 11th of August, you replied as follows:.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, over the next two days, did you return to the forced labour or to required labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Messengers came, and I was already -- I had already gone round a bend and I didn't care. I was telling them: "You can do whatever you want with me. You can kill me. My husband has already been taken away. I'm not going to do any work."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did this mean that you could just as well not go Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to your work obligation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once I didn't go, then they came for me and forced me to go, but that's probably why I was sent to Zasavica, on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You responded to a question by one of my colleagues, on page 25, line 8. The question was: "Did you go to do your work obligation?" And you said, "I stopped after the 11th of August because I had to take care of my husband."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that I -- the reason why I didn't go? Well, as a matter of fact, I didn't go only for a couple of days, because I was taking care of my husband. Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were testifying yesterday, you said that you didn't work all the time, every day, as part of your work obligation. You would go there and some people would be called out, some wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way it happened. After 15 days you wouldn't be called out once.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you were required to gather outside at the local commune between 7.00 and 8.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the local commune building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I said: Outside. You said your son didn't start with his work obligation right away [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son had his work obligation assignment on his own -- at his own workplace. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. That was his normal job. That was my son's employer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. That's how it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will try to rephrase, to reformulate what you've just told me, and you tell me if that's correct. [redacted] [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was sometime in May, but whether it was the 10th or the 15th, I don't know. It's not an important date at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. After that, he worked in a labour brigade. You said that he went to milk cows first, then to dig trenches, and had other work assignments. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Until the August of 1992, did your son spend around 30 days with that labour brigade? Is it approximately that figure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he had two or three days off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In response to a Prosecutor's question, you said that as far as you knew, that work obligation was not something for which you received pay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. No one in my family received any pay for work duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [redacted], did he receive a salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]. During the first days, he already lost all that he had, and in -- and even the SDK wasn't functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But did he promise to pay all his employees once things get back to normal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. I didn't know it would come to this, but I would have brought my son, his labour booklet or card, where the last entry is dated the 31st of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, madam, the doctors whose names you've just read on those three documents, did they receive salaries for their work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking too much. I saw Dr. Damir on one occasion, Dr. Mira -- Ruza, sorry. I didn't ask whether they were being paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. Speculation to ask her whether these three doctors that she had seen or for treatment were being paid. He can ask her if they were paid for treatment, or something along those lines, but whether they were getting paid by the state is outside of her knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I posed the question: Do you know, to the best of your knowledge, whether these doctors received their salaries. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but even if you ask "do you know," is it normal for people to go telling other people their salaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I was asking the witness only just about her knowledge. She answered: I don't know. And that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a waste of time to ask such questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, when we receive the answer, that is the only time when we know whether we wasted the time or not, with all due respect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, that's not the way you conduct your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I'm sorry, but I'm really trying my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a waste of time to ask such a question from a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I will insist that it was a waste of time, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move to another topic. Your husband was arrested on the 11th of August, 1992, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that day, around 7.00 p.m., as you've stated here, you went to see Milan Simic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you saw him outside, and he told you to come back in the morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and he gave me a lift home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next day when you came to see him in the morning, he took you to his office, and that's where you sat down; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And he left the office to go and see what the problem was with your husband; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said that on that occasion he spoke to Savo Cancarevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he ran into Savo Cancarevic at the entrance to the assembly and that both of them went back to his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Savo Cancarevic was then the commander of the police, and he still is; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The chief of police then was Stevo Todorovic; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly when you said that having spoken to Savo Cancarevic, Milan came to the office where you were sitting and told you that -- in the transcript of the 28th November, page 12, unofficial transcript, line 21: [In English] "He told me: [redacted], the proceedings are under way, to which I replied: I know, Milan, that proceedings are under way. I didn't come here to hear that, sweetheart. [redacted] [redacted]. And that is how we parted. He was looking down at his feet, and I left in tears."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to make one correction. He and Mr. Cancarevic were not talking. They just ran into each other at the door. Milan came Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. right to the door and Savo was coming into the building of the municipality, so they went together to his office, and we were there together for that short while. Maybe they had greeted each other, maybe they exchanged a couple of words. I didn't see that. I only saw Mr. Milan Simic turning away from the door and Mr. Cancarevic coming up to the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, Savo Cancarevic was together with Milan Simic in the office when Milan was telling you that the proceedings were under way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did Savo Cancarevic confirm that statement, since he was commander of the police, he was informed, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if he greeted me on that day, but I would have remembered if he had said anything else. He didn't address me at all. He probably said hello. He is a well-mannered man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you said that Milan Simic was looking down, can you tell us what you think that meant, to the best of your ability? If you don't know, tell us that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, after seeing Milan Simic, and after he told you that proceedings were under way, and after the way you parted, you went to see some other people, like Simo Bozic, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's 1700 hours, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will rise and the proceedings will continue tomorrow morning at 0930 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 30th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
